artifacts.title: cvprofiles
artifacts.summary: A Python package that treats construct validity as partial identification over a menu of measurement functions. Given a researcher-authored nomological network, the engine returns the admissible measurement set M* and a construct-identified range [L,U] for a target functional — empty sets and wide ranges are reported as findings, not failures.
details: Pure numpy/pandas computation over the score columns you supply: no GPU, no model weights, no API keys.

A profile is always the same four plain-text files — scores, roles, a nomological network with thresholds θ, and the target functional β — so every run is fully specified, hash-stamped, and replayable.
One-command teaching bundle (cvprofiles demo) writes an HTML report plus a JSON summary carrying the scores, network, and β hashes.
Bootstrap bands, θ- and δ-grids, and a units-split holdout are additive diagnostics that never replace the headline range; the P4b holdout promotes the robust admissible set instead.
v3.0.2 (Aug 2026) is a reproducibility patch: round-trip CSV parsing and the F1–F8 audit closeout, following the named empty-R unrestricted-multiverse case added in 3.0.1.
Installable from PyPI (pip install cvprofiles), MIT licensed, CI on every push; version tags act as frozen paper anchors.

credit.authored: The identification framing, the nomological-network protocol, the admissibility and gating rules, and the decision that empty sets and wide ranges ship as results.
credit.assisted: My hermes agent drove implementation of the engine, CLI, and reporting surface against that specification, under my review.
credit.verification: Frozen, tagged release runs with machine-readable proof summaries; CI on every push; synthetic-only claims labelled provisional rather than presented as paper results.

artifacts.title: LeanEcon v4
artifacts.summary: A clean-room rebuild of LeanEcon: an economics-formalization collaborator that takes an English claim through reviewed interpretation, Lean 4 formalization, and kernel-checked verification — emitting an auditable verification bundle and replayable trace instead of a bare "it compiles" claim.
details: Current release v2.0.0 "Phoenix": the v1 verified workflow plus measured AI-reviewer exercise and audit-gated assist libraries (bounded revision loop, proof-skeleton contract).
A claim is only labelled VERIFIED when the formal statement compiles in a pinned Lean 4 + Mathlib workspace with no sorry and passes the complete 12-check bundle validator, axiom audit included.

Interpretation (mistral-medium-3-5) and formalization (labs-leanstral-1-5) run live; semantic approval stays with an accountable reviewer under an explicit reviewer policy. Models draft, they do not certify.
Ships explicit non-claims next to the promises: no autonomous VERIFIED, no production SLA, no B2 auto-prove, and a formalizer that is not yet statement-faithful.
Runs the agent-attribution experiment: the hermes agent commits under its own GitHub account, so the human/agent split is recorded in the commit history rather than self-reported.
Supersedes LeanEcon v3, frozen as an immutable experimental record; every relationship to a v3 artifact is logged in a migration ledger with an explicit disposition.

credit.authored: Product thesis, the verification contract (what VERIFIED is allowed to mean), reviewer policy, Core scope, bundle validator checks, and the explicit non-claims list.
credit.assisted: My hermes agent commits implementation work under its own GitHub account, so the human/agent split is visible in the commit history rather than asserted here.
credit.verification: Lean kernel type-checking in a pinned workspace, a 12-check bundle validator, axiom/dependency audit, and replayable run traces.

artifacts.title: Synthetic Cultural Agents from Aggregate Anchors
artifacts.subtitle: SCA 2.0 proof-of-work
artifacts.summary: A falsifiable construction protocol for population-level choice policies. The pipeline renders declared aggregate anchors — country-level Global Preference Survey scores — into synthetic preference data, fits country-specific DPO/QLoRA adapters on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and evaluates the induced policies against independent human survey distributions.
details: Country labels are excluded from primary inference prompts: culture enters through the training signal, not through prompt retrieval.

The protocol predeclares five rejection points — anchor transmission, policy encoding, a permuted-anchor placebo for anchor relevance, external transport to independent human evidence, and operator robustness.
Ships the full stack: synthetic generation with scoring and QC, the canonical DPO training pipeline, and a World Values Survey out-of-sample evaluation surface with result tables.

Methods working paper (Gonzalez-Bonorino, Biriukova, Capra) includes a USA/MEX pilot diagnostic and an independent adversarial audit of the generation pipeline; results shells await the scaled experiment.

credit.authored: The construction protocol, the scope boundary, the five predeclared rejection points, and the multi-country experimental design — plus the methods paper with my co-authors.
credit.assisted: My hermes agent drove pipeline implementation, training scripts, and evaluation harness against that specification; the human/agent split is visible in the commit history.
credit.verification: Predeclared rejection points, a permuted-anchor placebo, out-of-sample evaluation against independent WVS human distributions, and an independent adversarial audit of the generation pipeline.
